name: Versace
why: Bold, decorated clothing — printed silk, gold hardware, the Medusa emblem.
origin: Founded in Milan in 1978 by Gianni Versace.

notes.ital: Calabrian by birth and Milanese by address, and the Medusa comes from the Magna Graecia ruins Gianni grew up among. Southern Italy read as ornament.
notes.status: Status as volume. The Medusa is not subtle, has never tried to be, and the wearer is not asking to be read quietly.

notes.craft: Versace's own former parent described its production as handled by independent third-party contractors, with materials going through a Novara warehouse. The only owned making space found is the made-to-measure atelier in Via Gesu, Milan. versace.com product pages give fiber content but no country, maker or mill (0/8). The only country-of-make statement is the filing's 'vast majority ... in Italy', so 2, not 4.

craft_evidence.owned_d: No owned production found. Former parent Capri Holdings' 10-K (FY2019 and FY2021, same wording): Versace 'has a centrally managed production model'; raw materials go to a central warehouse in Novara, Italy (owned by Versace, run by a third party) and 'are distributed to independent third-party manufacturing contractors'. The only owned making space found is the made-to-measure Atelier inside Palazzo Versace, Via Gesu 12, Milan (described in Apritimoda open-house text as hosting offices, the made-to-measure Atelier and showrooms) - couture/MTM only, not the range. Ownership: Prada S.p.A. completed the acquisition from Capri on 2 Dec 2025; no Prada statement found about moving Versace production into Prada-owned factories (Prada says only that Versace is 'part of this industrial platform logic').
craft_evidence.countries: No country on any PDP: 0/8 (sample of 8 on versace.com US: cotton poplin shirt, silk shirt, wool polo sweater, wool cardigan, straight jeans, wool-stretch blazer, suede-shearling blouson, leather pants; full-text check of blazer page found no 'Made in'/'Italy'). Capri 10-K FY2021: 'vast majority of Versace's production is located in Italy', remainder elsewhere in EMEA and a small portion in Asia (FY2019: Turkey, Tunisia, elsewhere in Europe, Asia).
